title: init --dry-run writes nothing, and a second init on a set-up repository writes nothing
assertion: In a git repository with a pyproject.toml and its own CLAUDE.md, `swerepo init --dry-run` exits 0, prints a plan with something to create, and leaves every file and folder unchanged (names, sizes, modification times and contents, `.git` included). After `swerepo init --yes` has applied it, a second `swerepo init --yes` exits 0, says "Nothing to do." and again leaves everything unchanged.

origin.text: Phase 3 behaviour (SWEREPO-SPEC §5 principles 1 and 6). Marked critical and swerepo/adr.py added to its scope on Gemini's recommendation (Phase 3 review, Q5 and P3-F07): a dry run that writes is as trust-breaking as check writing. Checked to fail when the dry run applies, or when init rewrites .swerepo.toml on every run. Proposed for the owner to approve.
